entries.title: Alternate Chase
entries.summary: A round-based pursuit subsystem using movement, speed modifiers, complications, successes, and setbacks.
entries.intro: The party that initiates the chase goes first.
entries.contentHtml:
Assumptions

  • Unless initiated in combat, the quarry starts between one and three Strides away.
  • The quarry continually uses all of its movement to get away.
  • People, walls, furniture, and other obstacles interrupt line of sight. The quarry is considered hidden during the chase.
  • If you can't use move actions—such as while immobilized, grabbed, restrained, or unconscious—you drop out of the chase.

Rounds

  • Each round represents 1 minute of pursuit.
  • Your turn represents moving as fast as possible in pursuit and ends with overcoming a complication.
  • You must use at least 1 action to move on your turn or drop out of the chase after that turn.
  • For every additional move action you use, gain +1 to your speed modifier.
  • If you can't move during your turn, you drop out of the chase.

Speed

  • The base Speed is the Speed of the slowest quarry.
  • For every 5 feet of difference between the base Speed and an individual's Speed, adjust that individual's speed modifier by 1: positive when faster than the base Speed and negative when slower.
  • Add your speed modifier to your complication check.

Complications

  • A complication is an event the participant must address, usually with a skill check. Saving throws may instead happen to the participant.
  • Failure uses up the participant's action.
  • Success leaves the participant with an action to use outside the complication.
  • Succeeding at the complication gives the participant one success.
  • Failing the complication gives the participant one setback.

Setbacks

  • You can tolerate a number of setbacks equal to your Constitution modifier or 1, whichever is higher.
  • For every setback beyond that limit, you gain the slowed condition.
  • If another chase participant damages you, you gain one setback.

Ending the Chase

Quarry

On the round after the quarry earns three successes, it has a chance to flee. The quarry makes an opposed check appropriate to its approach: Athletics to keep running, Stealth to hide, Society to work through a city, Survival to slip through the woods, and so on.

The check is made against the closest pursuer—the pursuer with the fewest setbacks. On a success, the quarry flees. On a failure, it faces the next complication with one fewer action because it used that action to flee.

Pursuers

On the round after a pursuer earns three successes, it can try to stop the quarry. If the pursuer prevents the quarry from taking move actions—for example by leaving it immobilized, grabbed, restrained, or unconscious—the chase ends.

If the quarry is adversarial, this leads to combat and the pursuers act first. If it is neutral or hospitable, this leads to conversation.

If the pursuer fails to prevent the quarry from moving, the pursuer faces the next complication with one fewer action because it used that action to stop the quarry.

entries.title: Venting & Submersion
entries.summary: Character-specific rules for WE4LAND's weight, underwater venting, overheating, and post-submersion corrosion.
entries.intro: WE4LAND's construction makes submersion a problem of buoyancy, heat management, and corrosion rather than ordinary breathing.
entries.contentHtml:
Weight & Buoyancy

  • Using aluminum as the assumed material density, WE4LAND weighs about three times as much as a typical person: 18 Bulk, approximately halfway between the Large and Huge Bulk guidelines.
  • Venting provides enough buoyancy that WE4LAND does not rapidly sink.
  • Venting functions only while WE4LAND is conscious and online.

Venting Underwater

WE4LAND's cooling system requires airflow and was designed for a thin upper atmosphere. When submerged or otherwise unable to vent, WE4LAND risks overheating.

Initial Capacity
7 rounds (5 + Constitution modifier)
End of Each Turn
Reduce remaining capacity by 1, or by 2 if WE4LAND attacked or Cast a Spell that turn
Critical Stress
Lose 1 additional round after each critical hit or critical failure against a damaging effect
At 0 Rounds
WE4LAND begins overheating

Rounds remaining: ______ / 7

Overheating

If WE4LAND takes any action while overheating, it must attempt a DC 20 Fortitude save at the end of that turn.

  • Failure WE4LAND takes 1d10 fire damage.
  • After the first check, the DC increases by 5 and the damage increases by 1d10 for each subsequent check.
  • These cumulative increases remain until maintenance is performed.
  • Maintenance can be performed only while WE4LAND is not submerged.

Corrosion

Immediately after leaving water or another polar substance, WE4LAND must spend at least 1 hour performing preventative maintenance and drying. If this is not done, roll 1d6 and apply the corresponding condition from the source's listed order.

1d6Condition
1Clumsy
2Drained
3Enfeebled
4Fatigued
5Off-Guard
6Slowed

If the result uses a condition value, that value begins at 1 and increases by 1 for each day without maintenance.

This short, broad-barrelled pistol uses a spring-loaded firing pin and a small black-powder charge to launch signal flares. Its brightly painted grip and unusually wide muzzle distinguish it from a conventional firearm.

A flare pistol can load only flare cartridges. It can't fire ordinary firearm ammunition, and flare cartridges can't be fired from other weapons. Because it is intended as emergency equipment, the pistol lacks the fatal and concussive traits common to many firearms. Its Strikes deal nonlethal fire damage.

Signal Shot ◆

Manipulate

Requirements You are wielding a loaded flare pistol containing a primed flare cartridge.

Fire the flare toward an unoccupied point in the air within 120 feet to which you have line of effect. No attack roll is required. The flare ignites there, shedding bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for another 20 feet for 1 minute. An airborne flare falls 10 feet at the end of each of your turns.

Creatures adjacent to the flare must succeed at a DC 15 Fortitude save or become dazzled until they are no longer adjacent to it. In clear conditions at night, the flare is readily visible at a great distance; the GM determines how weather, daylight, terrain, buildings, and other obstructions affect its visibility.

entries.contentHtml:
Ancestry
Azarketi
Heritage
Benthic Azarketi
Class
Oracle
Background
Otherworldly Mission
Level
3

Current Features

  1. Divine Spellcasting

    Oracle Feature

    Oziza casts divine spells spontaneously using Charisma and a spell repertoire.

  2. Cosmos Mystery

    Oracle Mystery

    Her mystery grants the Nature skill, cosmic spells, and the Spray of Stars revelation spell.

  3. Curse of the Sky's Call

    Oracular Curse

    While cursebound, Oziza is enfeebled by her cursebound value and takes an equal status penalty against forced movement.

  4. Revelation Spells

    Oracle Feature

    Revelation spells are focus spells tied to Oziza's mystery and automatically heighten with her level.

  5. Oracular Curse

    Oracle Feature

    Cursebound abilities increase her cursebound value; Refocusing reduces it and restores a Focus Point.

  6. Signature Spells

    Oracle Feature

    One spell of each available rank is a signature spell and can be heightened freely.

  7. Low-Light Vision

    Azarketi Feature

    Oziza sees in dim light as though it were bright light and ignores concealment caused only by dim light.

  8. Hydration

    Azarketi Feature

    She normally must submerge once every 24 hours; her campaign-granted Rehydration feat provides another way to satisfy this need.

Current Feats

  1. Oracular Warning

    Awarded Feat · Level 1

    Free Action—Trigger: you roll initiative. Allies within 20 feet gain a +2 status bonus to initiative and temporary HP equal to half your level for 1 minute. The initiative bonus rises to +3 at cursebound 2 and +4 at cursebound 3.

  2. Benthic Azarketi

    Heritage · Level 1

    Gain cold resistance equal to half your level. Wet conditions don't make environmental cold more severe for you, and abrupt changes in water pressure have no harmful effect.

  3. Hydraulic Deflection

    Ancestry Feat · Level 1

    One Action—Raise a moving sheet of water that grants a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn.

  4. Bargain Hunter

    Skill Feat · Level 2

    Use Diplomacy to Earn Income by finding bargains. When you buy an item, reduce its price by the income you earned; if selected during character creation, begin with 2 additional gp.

  5. Cantrip Expansion

    Class Feat · Level 2

    Add two extra cantrips from the oracle spell list to your spell repertoire.

  6. Untrained Improvisation

    General Feat · Level 3

    Add a proficiency bonus to untrained skill checks: level – 2 now, level – 1 at 5th level, and your full level at 7th. This does not permit actions that require trained proficiency.

  7. Rehydration

    Campaign-Granted Feat · Level 1

    Free at character creation. Once per day, spend 1 hour resting to draw moisture from the air; this counts as submerging in water for Hydration. It might fail in exceptionally dry areas at the GM's discretion.

entries.contentHtml:
Ancestry
Goblin
Heritage
Changeling
Class
Animist
Background
Herbalist
Level
3

Current Features

  1. Apparition Attunement

    Animist Feature

    During daily preparations, Ritsa attunes to two apparitions and designates one as her primary apparition.

  2. Animist & Apparition Spellcasting

    Animist Feature

    She prepares divine animist spells and spontaneously casts spells supplied by her attuned apparitions.

  3. Vessel Spells

    Animist Feature

    Her primary apparition supplies a vessel focus spell; changing the primary apparition while Refocusing changes the vessel spell available.

  4. Shaman

    Animistic Practice

    Ritsa forms unusually close bonds that let an apparition inhabit a familiar's physical form.

  5. Invocation of Embodiment

    Shaman Feature

    This grants Spirit Familiar at 1st level and Enhanced Familiar at 2nd level.

  6. Primary Apparition

    Animist Feature

    The primary apparition grants its vessel spell and can be changed among currently attuned apparitions when Ritsa Refocuses.

  7. Second Apparition

    Animist Feature

    The second attuned apparition contributes Lore and apparition spells even while it is not primary.

  8. Darkvision

    Goblin Feature

    Ritsa can see in darkness and dim light, though darkness remains black and white.

  9. Fortitude Expertise

    Animist Feature

    At 3rd level, Ritsa's Fortitude save proficiency increases to expert.

Current Feats

  1. Spirit Familiar

    Awarded Feat · Level 1

    During daily preparations, manifest one attuned apparition as a familiar. If it is destroyed, you lose the other benefits of that apparition until your next daily preparations; dispersing the apparition also destroys the familiar.

  2. Natural Medicine

    Awarded Feat · Level 1

    Use Nature instead of Medicine to Treat Wounds, including higher DCs allowed by your Nature proficiency. This substitution doesn't cover other Medicine actions or prerequisites; fresh wilderness ingredients can grant a +2 circumstance bonus.

  3. Enhanced Familiar

    Awarded Feat · Level 2

    During daily preparations, choose four familiar or master abilities for your familiar instead of two.

  4. Alchemical Crafting

    Awarded Feat · Level 2

    You can use Craft to create alchemical items and immediately gain formulas for four common 1st-level alchemical items.

  5. Changeling

    Heritage · Level 1

    Gain the changeling trait and access to changeling ancestry feats. The heritage normally grants low-light vision, or darkvision if you already have low-light vision; Ritsa's goblin darkvision already covers this sense.

  6. Dream May

    Ancestry Feat · Level 1

    Gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saves against sleep and dream effects. A full night's rest restores HP equal to twice your level × Constitution modifier and reduces drained and doomed by 2 instead of 1.

  7. Battle Medicine

    Skill Feat · Level 2

    One Action—With a healer's toolkit, attempt the Treat Wounds DC to restore the same HP in combat. It doesn't remove wounded, and that target becomes immune to your Battle Medicine for 1 day; this immunity is separate from Treat Wounds.

  8. Herbalist Dedication

    Class Feat · Level 2

    Gain advanced alchemy for healing consumables, preparing four daily items minus two when outside the wilderness. Become expert in Nature, remember qualifying formulas, and can use Nature plus a healer's toolkit to Craft healing alchemical consumables.

  9. Untrained Improvisation

    General Feat · Level 3

    Add a proficiency bonus to untrained skill checks: level – 2 now, level – 1 at 5th level, and your full level at 7th. This does not permit actions that require trained proficiency.

  10. Bone Magic

    Ancestry Feat · Level 3

    Gain guidance as an occult innate cantrip usable at will. It automatically heightens to a rank equal to half your level, rounded up.

    Automaton Feature

    WE4LAND need not eat, drink, or sleep, but needs 2 hours of aware standby each day or becomes fatigued. He still needs breathable air to vent magical exhaust.

Inside is a peculiar self-sustaining alchemical culture of eggs, spores, nutrient paste, and substances its inventor isn't confident they can identify. When properly tended, the culture produces a steady—but thankfully very small—supply of edible insects.

Feed the Culture ◆

During your daily preparations, place a negligible amount of edible organic material in the crock, such as a bread crumb, vegetable shred, dried herb, or ration scrap. The culture produces one harmless Tiny insect: a beetle, cricket, cockroach, grub, mealworm, moth, or similar creature.

It is sterile, has no monetary value, cannot produce useful venom, poison, reagents, or other valuable substances, and has no attacks or mechanically significant abilities. If uneaten, it dies harmlessly at the beginning of your next daily preparations.

entries.title: House Rules for Players
entries.summary: Twenty-one consolidated campaign rulings for players, including revival, ABP, item, and table-play conventions.
entries.intro: The player-facing source of truth for Gaileia's campaign-wide rules.
entries.source: Feedback for Homebrew GitHub Site | Tabletop Projects – Feedback 6; Session Zero Preface | PF2; Homebrew Rules | PF2; Mechanics Codex
entries.contentHtml:
These 21 rulings collect the campaign-wide player rules identified in the homebrew rules review and Session Zero Primer.

Magic, Revival, and Items

  1. Meaningful Revival Costs

    The normal valuables required by reincarnate, resurrect, raise dead, and similar magic are replaced by a meaningful tribute or sacrifice. Player characters pay no component cost when they cast the magic themselves; hiring an NPC still requires paying for spellcasting service.

  2. Accessible Scroll Casting

    A player character can attempt to cast from a scroll even when the spell is not on their spell list by succeeding at a DC 16 flat check.

  3. Spherical Areas

    On a physical battle mat, spell areas that would normally be spheres are treated as cylinders for measurement and template placement.

  4. Magic-Item Sizing

    Magic items do not automatically resize to fit their wearer or wielder.

  5. Magic-Item Wear

    Magic items are subject to ordinary damage, maintenance, and wear.

  6. Repairing Magic Items

    Mending can affect a magic item when the caster has Magical Crafting and succeeds at that item's Crafting DC.

Automatic Bonus Progression

  1. Campaign ABP

    The campaign uses Automatic Bonus Progression. Fundamental potency, striking, and resilient runes—and equivalent permanent numerical bonuses from magical items—are replaced by character progression.

  2. Temporary Item Bonuses

    Temporary item bonuses still apply normally.

  3. Bombs and ABP

    Alchemical bombs benefit from ABP attack potency, but they do not gain additional weapon-damage dice from ABP.

  4. Gate Attenuators

    Gate attenuators are treated as nonmagical for this campaign's ABP interaction.

  5. Major Gate Attenuators

    Major gate attenuators do not grant their normal Apex attribute boost.

  6. Runesmith Conversion

    A weapon’s property-rune capacity equals the wielder’s current ABP attack-potency value. Runesmith runes remain separate and consume no property-rune slots.

Characters and Table Play

  1. Nonlethal by Default

    Damage dealt by a player character is nonlethal by default unless that player declares otherwise.

  2. Private Character Knowledge

    Information about a character remains private until that character shares it in play.

  3. Secret Social Conflict

    Opposed social checks between player characters are resolved through trust and roleplay. Secret checks are reserved for situations in which the characters genuinely mistrust one another.

  4. Physical Player Conflict

    Physical conflict between player characters requires serious narrative justification and group consent.

  5. Survival Resources

    Food, water, and related survival resources are tracked while the party is outside civilization; use the Survival rules when they become relevant.

  6. NPC Construction

    NPCs and monsters do not have to follow player-character construction rules, including PC action economy, magic, death, class features, or ancestry abilities.

  7. Flexible Features and Flavour

    Players can propose flavourful changes to features. Mechanical changes require a conversation and GM approval.

  8. Unique Character Options

    A class or ancestry might be unique in the setting or to a particular character. Two player characters can still share a class when the group agrees it fits.

  9. Potions

    Potions are alchemical and nonmagical unless a specific item says otherwise.

Spell Mechanics

Bringing Characters Back

The normal valuables required by reincarnate, resurrect, raise dead, and similar magic are replaced with a meaningful tribute or sacrifice. The offering should be narratively important rather than a simple wealth tax.

Possible tributes include sacrificing a limb, a favored weapon, another life, or a commissioned likeness of the deceased. There are intentionally no hard-and-fast rules: be creative and make the cost matter to the story.

These spells have no component cost when cast by a player character. Hiring an NPC to cast one still requires paying for the NPC's spellcasting service.

Four Aspects of a Soul

The Mechanics Codex makes the tribute concrete: returning a creature to life can use up to four aspects of that creature—one each representing emotion, imagination, memory, and sense. The normal strict secondary-caster requirement is removed. Each contributor performs an appropriate secondary check, with room for the GM to approve another skill.

  • A failed check consumes the aspect used for it; that aspect can't be used in another attempt.

Primary Check
Nature (expert)
Secondary Checks
Occultism, Religion, or GM discretion
Range & Target
10 feet; one dead creature up to 8th level that died within the past week

This renamed version of reincarnate returns the soul in a new body. Roll 1d20 for its ancestry category: 1–14 produces a common ancestry; 15–20 produces an uncommon or rare ancestry. The GM selects regionally appropriate possibilities and randomly determines the result.

  • Critical Success The target returns in an adult body at full Hit Points, with the spells and pool points it had when it died.
  • Success The target returns at 1 Hit Point with no prepared spells or pool points and is clumsy 2, drained 2, and enfeebled 2 for 1 week. These conditions can't be reduced early.
  • Failure The target does not return.
  • Critical Failure The soul becomes trapped in an unintelligent animal no higher than half the target's level, with Intelligence 1 (–5), and can't use its own abilities.

Heightening Maximum target level: 10 at 4th rank; 12 at 5th; 14 at 6th (dead no longer than 1 month); 16 at 7th (1 month); 18 at 8th (1 year); 20 at 9th (1 decade).

Resurrection

Cast
1 day; up to 4 aspects
Primary Check
Religion (expert)
Secondary Checks
Medicine, Society, or GM discretion
Range & Target
10 feet; one dead creature up to 10th level that died within the past year
  • Critical Success The target returns at full Hit Points with the spells and pool points it had when it died, retains long-term debilitations, and gains a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, Perception, saves, and skill checks for 1 week.
  • Success The target returns at 1 Hit Point with no prepared spells or pool points, retains long-term debilitations, and is clumsy 1, drained 1, and enfeebled 1 for 1 week. These conditions can't be reduced early.
  • Failure The attempt is unsuccessful.
  • Critical Failure Something goes horribly wrong, such as possession, undeath, or another fate chosen by the GM.

Heightening Maximum target level: 12 at 6th rank; 14 at 7th (dead no longer than 1 decade); 16 at 8th; 18 at 9th (dead no longer than 1 century); 20 at 10th (no death-time limit).

Raise Dead

Cast
10 minutes; up to 4 aspects
Primary Check
Religion (expert)
Range & Target
10 feet; one dead creature up to 13th level that died within the past 3 days

On a successful return, the creature has 1 Hit Point, no prepared spells, spell slots, pool points, or other daily resources, and retains any long-term debilitations. It is clumsy 2, drained 2, and enfeebled 2 for 1 week; these conditions can't be reduced early.

Heightening Maximum target level: 15 at 7th rank; 17 at 8th; 19 at 9th; 21 at 10th.

Scrolls

A player character can attempt to cast a scroll with a DC 16 flat check. This keeps scrolls usable in a group without an appropriate spellcaster and creates a dramatic choice between using a scroll now or saving it to learn later.

Spell Areas

When playing on a physical mat, spell areas that would otherwise be spheres are treated as cylinders. This keeps measurement and template placement simple and imaginable at the table.

Specific Spells

Mending

Mending can affect a magic item when the caster has the Magical Crafting feat and succeeds at the Crafting DC for that item.

Item Mechanics

Magic items do not automatically adjust to a creature's size and are not immune to ordinary damage and wear.

This creates useful reasons for martial characters to spend money and for characters to invest in Crafting.

entries.title: Ritsa's Nature for Medicine
entries.summary: Ritsa can substitute Nature for specific medical checks while still meeting Medicine proficiency prerequisites normally.
entries.intro: A campaign-specific expansion of Ritsa's natural healing practice.
entries.source: Feedback for Homebrew GitHub Site | Tabletop Projects – Feedback 6
entries.contentHtml:
Prerequisites

Ritsa must meet all Medicine proficiency prerequisites normally. Substituting Nature for a check does not change which proficiency a feat or action requires.

Nature Substitution

When Ritsa provides medical treatment or first aid through natural methods, she can roll Nature in place of the Medicine check. This includes:

  • using Nature to Administer First Aid;
  • qualifying for and performing Battle Medicine with Nature; and
  • using Unusual Treatment with Nature.
